_comment: Rated per-port protocol-session and flow capacity, from the Athena performance
This file overrides the matrix compiled into the tests. It is optional: delete
it and both tests fall back to their built-in table, which holds these same
numbers. It is picked up automatically from this directory by bgpv4/ and
Every run logs which table it used and every row this file changed, so the log
always records where an enforced limit came from. A file that exists but does
not parse is a fatal error rather than a silent fall back to the built-ins.
Fields are optional per row: omit one and the built-in value is kept. Note that
0 is NOT 'omitted' -- it means 'not rated', which disables the check for that
'aresone' is a whole-resource-group total, split evenly over however many ports
the group is broken out into: 1x800G 36556, 2x400G 18278, 4x200G 9139,
8x100G 4570, 16x50G 2285. Every other row is a flat per-port figure.
OPEN QUESTION on novus_normal: the performance matrix screenshot reads
35686 / 31334. The 36556 / 26982 below was an explicit instruction, to rate the
Novus 10G card the same as an unsplit AresONE group. Change the two numbers
here to follow the published matrix instead -- no code change needed.
_cards_comment: 'cards' rates cards the built-in matching rules do not cover. Each entry is:
the first match wins over every
"per_group": false,                 true = bgpv4/bgpv6 are a whole-group
total to split over the group's port
"source":    "why this rating"      quoted in the run log
